name: drive-paid-receipts-to-table

trigger.authentication_note: Google Drive dennis@work.flowers. The SAME connection is needed twice: here on the trigger (which polls the folder) and as the `gdrive` alias in --connections, because the workflow code renames the file.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger (New File in Folder), one run per file added to the Paid Receipts folder. No webhook_url — nothing external needs a catch URL, so cutover is just turning the classic Zap off.

connectionless_apps.AICLIAPI: get_completion — authentication_id "0" (Included in Plan), no connection
connectionless_apps.TableCLIAPI: search_or_write/find_record + write/update_record — Zapier Tables need no connection

receipts.name: [Table] Receipts
receipts.role: Sole owner. One row per receipt file, keyed on File ID (f1).
receipts.datetime_note: f5 (Date) is written as `<invoiceDate>T00:00:00Z` — a bare YYYY-MM-DD is read in the account's local timezone and silently shifts.

ai_model.note: Tier drives task cost: standard 1x, advanced 3x, premium 5x tasks per run. Standard correctly extracted vendor/date/currency/amount from a real receipt (Anthropic, PBC) tested via run-action on 2026-07-28 — see the README's verified-cases table. This step makes no tool calls, which is the main reason Zapier's own default is Advanced.
ai_model.file_input_note: The PDF is passed to the model as a file input (inputFieldConfig_Invoice_isFileUrl), using the Drive trigger's `file` hydrate reference.

description: Google Drive receipt PDF added to Paid Receipts -> AI by Zapier extracts vendor/date/currency/amount -> rename file '<invoice date> <vendor>' -> find-or-create its row in the [Table] Receipts Zapier Table, keyed on file ID, then sync the Table's File Name field to the file's actual post-rename title. Migration of the classic Zap 'Google Drive receipts processing and analysis'.
determinism_note: The workflow body runs in the durable runtime's GUARDED mode, where the `Date` constructor is proxied and its `construct` trap throws DeterminismViolation *before* inspecting its arguments — so even a deterministic `new Date(Date.UTC(y, m, d))` is rejected. This Zap shipped with two such calls (a NaN check inside `toIsoDate`, and a `?? new Date()` fallback for a missing receipt date) and would have failed on the first receipt PDF; it had had no runs, so the fault was latent rather than observed. Date handling is now integer arithmetic and the clock is read inside a `today` step. Verified against native `Date` over 1970..2100 before publishing.

version_history.note: Initial migration. Carried a latent DeterminismViolation — see determinism_note. Never ran.

Fix the guarded-mode `new Date()` calls: integer date arithmetic, clock moved into a `today` step. `toIsoDate` now genuinely rejects an impossible date (the old NaN check never fired, because Date.UTC normalises overflow instead of failing).
